images.caption: Figure 1:Drift under identity editing.Repeatedly instructing a model to leave the image unchanged exposes model-induced errors that accumulate across turns, and similar degradation occurs across different editing models.

Figure 2:Overview of MT-OPSD.The student first constructs self-generated rollout states by repeatedly applying the identity instruction.
For each rollout stateI~(k)\tilde{I}^{(k)}, the identity branch uses the state itself as the target underℒid\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{id}}, while the editing branch aligns the student conditioned onI~(k)\tilde{I}^{(k)}with a frozen teacher conditioned on the clean sourceI(0)I^{(0)}via sparse query-based velocity matchingℒedit\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{edit}}.
A rollout curriculum progressively increases the rollout depth, and improved student checkpoints replace the teacher through gated promotion.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on LME-Bench.Repeated editing leads to distinct failure patterns across backbones, while the training-free baselines either inherit these artifacts or weaken the requested edits.
MT-OPSD remains stable through 10 turns and continues to follow the editing sequence across all three backbones.
